reason: Strata lists NTFS's own metadata files ($MFT, $Bitmap, $Boot, ...) in the root, as FTK Imager and X-Ways do, so they can be examined; libfsntfs leaves them out of the root's listing. A choice of presentation, not a content difference.

The fixture deliberately declares 5000 bytes on a corrupt cluster chain that loops (17 -> 18 -> 17). Strata follows the chain for the declared size and notes the damage; libfsfat refuses to read it. Both are defensible on corrupt input.

libfsext refuses an entry of the synthetic ext4 image whose in-inode extended attribute area (inline data) it considers out of bounds. Not yet established whether the builder or either reader is wrong; kept here so the ext4 tree is not compared until it is looked at.

The private metadata folder's name begins with four NUL characters. Strata keeps them as they are on disk; libfshfs replaces each with the symbol for NUL (U+2400), so the same folder has two spellings. Content identical.
The same folder as the entry above, as libfshfs names it.

libfshfs does not apply HFS+ transparent compression (decmpfs) and reports the files as empty; Strata decompresses them. Strata's output is the one covered by its own decmpfs tests against known-good vectors.
The builder writes 8-sector grains so the fixtures stay tiny; libvmdk accepts only grains of more than 8 sectors (real writers use 128). Strata reads the image; the reference refuses it.

qemu-img works the disk size out from the CHS geometry in the footer, and a fixture of 40 sectors has zero cylinders, so it reports an empty disk. Strata and libvhdi both use the size the footer states. Needs a larger fixture to compare on.
The same: qemu-img converts an empty disk, so there is nothing to compare.
The builder writes no reference count table, which qemu requires and Strata and libqcow do not. A fixture shortcoming, not a difference in what the image holds.
The builder uses 4 KiB blocks to stay small; qemu accepts only the 1 MiB block size real writers use. Strata reads the image.
The fixture's blocks are LZFSE-compressed and qemu-img's LZFSE module is not installed, so it cannot read them. Strata decodes LZFSE against known-good vectors.
